description: Hey! I'm Karen, leading team Sisyphus. I focus on mechanical engineering, physics, and CAD prototyping . We’re turning microgravity fire data into an engineered suppression mechanism. Looking for teammates skilled in: Python / Data Science (analyzing NASA combustion datasets), UI/UX design, or technical storytelling & video pitch. Let’s build an ambitious project together
summary: In microgravity, buoyancy-driven convection disappears: flames become spherical, smoke fails to rise toward ceiling detectors, and invisible low-temperature "cool flames" (observed in NASA's FLEX experiments) can burn undetected while carbon monoxide accumulates silently. Flame in Freefall is an interactive, node-based spacecraft fire-safety simulator and differential trade-off engine grounded in 41 empirical NASA flight experiments. Using a directed multi-network blueprint workspace (OUT -> IN), mission engineers can model parallel cabin atmospheres in real time, scrub through a 600-second 2D finite-volume flame and hull thermal simulation, benchmark results against NASA Saffire, BASS-II, and FLEX telemetry, and isolate physical safety deltas between competing spacecraft designs via a two-pin AI Diff Comparator.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Flame in Freefall is an interactive, browser-based spacecraft fire-safety simulator and multi-network trade-off workbench grounded in 41 empirical NASA microgravity flight experiments. In microgravity (0g), buoyancy-driven convection vanishes: flames turn spherical, smoke fails to rise toward ceiling detectors, and invisible low-temperature "cool flames" (650–780 K, discovered in NASA FLEX / PSI-117) can silently consume oxygen and generate toxic carbon monoxide without triggering optical sensors.

To solve this, we engineered a visual Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) workspace (OUT -> IN) that allows mission engineers and flight controllers to run multiple independent cabin configurations side-by-side without state cross-contamination:

1. NOTE AI // JARVIS ARCHITECT: Compiles natural-language mission prompts or historical flight presets into physical boundary conditions.

2. ENV VARIABLES: Controls oxygen concentration (10–100% O₂), cabin pressure (0.30–2.00 atm), ECLSS ventilation airflow velocity (0–70 cm/s), compartment volume (10–200 m³), and fuel chemistry (PMMA solid acrylic, Sibal cotton-fiberglass fabric, n-Heptane, Hydrogen H₂, and Methane CH₄).

3. SIM 2D // FINITE-VOLUME SOLVER (0–600s): Real-time transient visualizer with time scrubbing across two modes—FLAME + O₂ FIELD (flame front expansion, downstream oxygen depletion wake, and ECLSS streamlines) and THERMAL HULL MAP (radiative and convective heat loading on the spacecraft pressure bulkhead).

4. SIM-TO-REAL // NASA PSI GROUNDING: Weighted multi-dimensional similarity engine (PARAMS, CURVE SHAPE, SAFETY RISK) calibrating live runs against 41 actual NASA experiments (Saffire I–VI, BASS-II, FLEX, ACME) and historical spaceflight anomalies (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir 1997).

5. GRAPH & TABLE // TELEMETRY MATRIX: Multi-channel time-series plots and searchable NASA PSI benchmark tables.

6. AI DIFF // COMPARATOR & AI BRIEF: Two-pin differential engine connecting Branch A and Branch B to isolate exact physical deltas (ΔVf, ΔTf, Δq''w, ΔP, Δ[CO]), score relative hazard reduction, and synthesize prioritized ECLSS countermeasures and a Flight Readiness Mission Brief.

PHYSICS & SAFETY FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Non-Equilibrium S-Curve & Extinction: Evaluates flow-to-chemical timescale ratios via the Damköhler number (Da) and Chung K. Law's ~15% O₂ microgravity flammability limit (LOI_crit) to classify EXTINCTION, COOL_BLUE, HOT_FLAME, and EXPLOSION_FLASH regimes.

- Structural & Toxicological Thresholds: Flags bulkhead thermal breach risk at q''w ≥ 28.0 kW/m², hull structural overpressure proof limits at ΔP ≥ 45.0 kPa (0.44 atm), and carbon monoxide toxicity at the 55 ppm 7-day Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentration (NASA JSC 20584 Rev D), while enforcing strict 0 ppm CO yield for carbon-free pure H₂ combustion.

- Scientific Transparency: Reconstructed telemetry curves are explicitly labeled alongside direct flight endpoints, and deterministic boundary invariants are verified via an automated test suite (scripts/verify_physics.js).

CREATIVITY, BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Unlike static spreadsheets or single-run 1g fire models, our node-based blueprint architecture turns complex microgravity combustion differential equations into an intuitive, zero-latency visual trade-off tool. Mission planners designing future commercial LEO stations, Lunar Gateway modules, or Artemis exploration habitats can immediately test how elevated oxygen atmospheres or ECLSS airflow changes affect hull thermal integrity and crew safety—preventing catastrophic fire scenarios before hardware is flown.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Frontend & Visualization: HTML5, CSS3 (SpaceX/NASA Mission Control Dark & Light themes), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas 2D Finite-Volume Renderer, and SVG Directed Graph Engine with desktop and touch gesture support.

- Physics & Verification Backend: Python 3 (combustion_model.py, optional FastAPI server, anomaly detection) and Node.js automated physics verification suite.

- Cloud & Version Control: Firebase Hosting (live zero-login deployment at https://microgravitational-flame.web.app) and GitHub.

- Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: Large Language Models and AI coding assistants were used to accelerate UI/CSS implementation, build automated boundary-condition unit tests, and synthesize English voiceover narration and SRT subtitles for the demonstration video. All combustion equations, physical thresholds, and NASA PSI dataset mappings were manually verified against primary NASA technical reports.
